title: Plasma metabolite classifiers distinguish psychiatric diagnoses in internal cohort testing
summary: A study of 1,609 adults with bipolar disorder, major depressive disorder, schizophrenia or healthy-control status identified 297 metabolites associated across diagnostic comparisons after age/sex adjustment and false-discovery correction. Classifiers including random forest and XGBoost evaluated diagnostic separation using randomly selected metabolite subsets in internal train/test splits. This is retrospective model evaluation of a single Han Chinese cohort whose samples were collected during 2018–2024; it does not establish causal mechanisms or clinical benefit. Medication effects were not explicitly assessed, and targeted metabolomics plus external multicenter validation are needed before diagnostic application.
ai_technology: Logistic regression, LASSO, random forest and XGBoost classifiers
organization: Suzhou Guangji Hospital; Soochow University; The University of Melbourne

evidence.tested: Internal diagnostic discrimination in a 70/30 train/test split and 10-fold training cross-validation across 1,609 participants; age/sex adjusted; random subsets of associated metabolites.
evidence.unknown: Medication effects were not explicitly assessed; lifestyle and illness-duration confounding, causal mechanisms, external multicenter performance and clinical utility remain unresolved.
evidence.ai_role: Supervised classifiers evaluated whether plasma metabolite subsets predict diagnostic groups; mutual-information feature associations are statistical screening, not AI.

source_review.scope: Publisher article-in-press full text: cohort, Methods, data split, mutual-information feature screen, model evaluation, Results, limitations and publication history.
